annotations.title: Cron Expression Next Runs (Vixie cron / cronie)

description: Explain a 5-field cron expression and list when it will next run. Send the expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, or @daily, @hourly and the other nicknames), the IANA time zone the cron daemon itself runs in (its TZ or system zone, e.g. America/Chicago; default UTC), a start date and time in that zone, and how many runs you want (1 to 50, default 10). Get back each field's values in plain words, whether the day-of-month OR day-of-week rule applies, and the next run times after the start, each with its local time, UTC offset and UTC instant. Runs that fall in a daylight-saving gap or in a repeated hour are said plainly, with what cronie does there. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/cron-next-runs). Not legal, tax or financial advice.

count.description: How many next runs to list, 1 to 50 (default 10).

expression.description: The schedule: 5 fields 'minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week' (e.g. '30 9 * * 1-5', '*/15 * * * *', '0 0 1,15 * *') or @yearly, @annually, @monthly, @weekly, @daily, @midnight, @hourly. No command part.

start_date.description: Start date in that zone, YYYY-MM-DD. Runs strictly after the start are listed.

start_time.description: Start time in that zone, 24-hour HH:MM.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone the cron daemon itself runs in (its TZ or the system zone), e.g. America/Chicago, Europe/Berlin. Default UTC. Not a crontab CRON_TZ (see does_not).
